subject: Short-term surge buffer & pricing playbook for Black Friday
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@atlasretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short-term capacity buffer for Black Friday

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — quick one from our side. We’re planning an expanded campaign for Black Friday that will likely push our query volumes well above our current committed baseline for a ~72-hour window. Historically our peak QPS tends to be ~3.2x baseline for a 36–48 hour spike, but this year we’re expecting longer tail traffic.

Can Redwood provide a short-term surge buffer or temporary quota uplift option and outline pricing/true-up mechanics? Specifically:
- Proposal for a short-term uplift (hours/days) and any minimum commitment
- Pricing for the uplift (ephemeral rate vs. overrun invoicing)
- Any onboarding/technical ramp requirements (we’d prefer a 48h warm-up)

I’ve attached last year’s usage export and a predicted spike CSV to help size this. Procurement may loop in a PO if we can get a succinct amendment.

Thanks — can you loop in the right folks?

— Olivia
Director, Platform Engineering
AtlasRetail

Attachment: atlas_bf_usage_summary.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term capacity buffer for Black Friday

Thanks Olivia — appreciate the context and the csv.

Short answer: yes, we can. We offer two practical paths depending on how Atlas wants to manage economics and invoicing:

1) Prepaid surge credits: you buy a bucket of surge credits (tokens/hour) that are consumed during the event. This gives predictable unit pricing and avoids surprise overrun invoices. Credits can be sized to your projected peak and refunded/prorated if unused per the amendment.

2) Ephemeral uplift (temporary quota increase): we spin a short-term quota uplift that increases your throughput ceilings for N hours/days. Usage during that period is billed at our surge rate; we then true-up usage at month-end.

If you want low friction and a clean PO path, prepaid credits + a short amendment usually works best. I’ve looped in Ben for pricing and Jordan for reconciliation/ops flow so we can propose a one-page amendment and an onboarding playbook.

Can you confirm the expected peak QPS and whether you prefer a prepaid credit model or invoiced true-up? Also confirm the PO contact for Procurement.

— Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Pricing options and example economics for short-term uplift

Hi Olivia / Marissa — thanks for the details. I ran a quick model against your usage CSV. Two options with sample economics:

A) Prepaid Surge Credits (recommended for PO-driven buyers)
- Buy surge credits that cover up to 2.5x baseline for a 96-hour window.
- Unit pricing: $0.28 per 1k tokens (surge bucket rate).
- Unused credits: pro-rata refund up to 30% of purchase, remainder converts to account credit.
- Benefit: predictable invoice, no ad-hoc overrun charges.

B) Ephemeral uplift + month-end true-up
- Temporary quota increase to 3x baseline for X hours.
- Usage during uplift billed at $0.42 per 1k tokens (overrun rate).
- Month-end reconciliation: any sustained uplift can convert to committed uplift with a 20% rebate applied retroactively if elected within 30 days.

We can also include a short grace window: if you notify us 72 hours in advance, we’ll hold the overrun rate at the lower band (A/B mid-rate) and waive surcharge.

I attached a simple pricing matrix and a draft one-page surge amendment that outlines the ramping clause, invoicing cadence, and a 30-day conversion option.

If you prefer a blended true-up (blended rates across baseline + uplift), we can propose that — Jordan, adding you to help define reconciliation windows and the blended calculator.

Attachments: proposed-surge-amendment-v1.pdf

— Ben
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@atlasretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing options and example economics for short-term uplift

Quick follow-up on ops and reconciliation:

- Reconciliation window: we recommend a 30-day true-up window after the event to allow accounting teams to validate telemetry. During that window we’ll provide token-level exports and a draft invoice.
- Blended/Cap option: for customers worried about sticker shock, we can do a blended cap — cap the maximum month-over-month uplift spend at X% over baseline; any excess becomes eligible for credit conversion if you sign a committed uplift within 30 days.
- Ramp / warm-up: we can support a 48-hour warm up as requested. For sustained warm-up we’ll route traffic to a warm pool to minimize cold-start latency.
- Legal/procurement asks: we’ll add a 48h ramp clause and a PO-friendly payment term (Net 30) to the amendment. Laura — can you confirm standard EULA addenda language for temporary amendments?

If Atlas prefers the prepaid route we’ll issue a one-page order form and a Docusign link for signature; if they prefer true-up we’ll lock the surge unit price and set the 30-day reconciliation.

Thanks — this reads well. Procurement reviewed both options and we’d like to proceed with the Prepaid Surge Credits path (option A) with the following asks before we sign:

1) Include a 48-hour ramp clause in the amendment (we’ll provide traffic patterns).
2) Put a modest refund floor: allow pro-rata refund for unused credits up to 40% (negotiable).
3) Include a one-time onboarding credit if Redwood provides a technical on-call for the first 24h of the event.

We’ve attached a placeholder PO to expedite internal approvals. If you can send the one-page order form + Docusign and the revised amendment with the ramp and refund language, we’ll aim to sign by EOD Friday.

Thanks — looping Procurement on the reply.
